nodes.label: Cluster Sharding
nodes.rationale: Entities are routed by hash(entityId) % numShards computed independently per node, so every correctness property in the subsystem hangs on the nodes agreeing about the modulus and about shard ownership.

nodes.label: Cluster Membership and Gossip
nodes.rationale: Membership is merged from peer-supplied records, so every field a peer can write is untrusted input: versions seeded from Date.now() make 'highest version wins' forgeable, and an unbounded member map is a remote memory sink.

nodes.label: HTTP Server Stack
nodes.rationale: Three interchangeable backends (Fastify, Express, Hono) must answer identically; every divergence between them has been a defect class of its own - different body caps, different path shapes, different refusal bodies.

nodes.label: HOCON Configuration
nodes.rationale: Precedence is explicit options > HOCON > built-in defaults; a key that ships in reference.conf but is read by nothing is a documented lie, which is why a test now walks every leaf.

nodes.label: Security-First Posture
nodes.rationale: Cap untrusted input at the boundary, never trust a client-supplied integrity field, credit the authenticated connection rather than the payload's self-description, and use crypto-grade randomness for anything that names a wire participant.

nodes.label: BREAKING: receptionist total cap renamed to maxSubscriptionsTotal (#1200)
nodes.rationale: The name moved rather than the implementation, because the pair count is the correct bound: re-pointing the check at distinct subscribers would have made the name true while removing a memory bound, since nothing caps keys per subscriber. Proven by applying the naive swap - a fourth subscribe from a capped-out subscriber succeeded while all three pre-existing total-cap tests stayed green, because each gave every subscriber exactly one key.

nodes.label: BREAKING: KeepMajority downs both sides of an exact 50/50 split (#1170)
nodes.rationale: Returning the empty set on a tie meant 'remain pending', but each side's view is stable once a partition settles, so pending was the permanent answer - the split-brain outcome the strategy exists to prevent. Both halves now run the same computation over their own view and down themselves, so the cluster stops whole instead of forking.

nodes.label: BREAKING: numShards mismatch is refused instead of double-homing entities (#633)
nodes.rationale: Two nodes configured differently put the same entity id in different shards at paths that never collide - for a persistent entity that is two writers on one persistenceId. RegisterRegion now carries numShards and the coordinator compares against its own configured count, not the first registrant's, because a leader change clears the region registry and the persisted coordinator state carries no shard count. Refusing registration alone was insufficient: GetShardHome never required one, so refused region keys are remembered and their requests dropped.

nodes.label: BREAKING: ActorCell handles a batch of user messages per dispatcher turn (#409)
nodes.rationale: Worth 2.1x-3.6x on tell throughput; the per-actor budget is exposed as ActorOptions.withThroughput() and actor-ts.actor.throughput so fairness stays tunable.

nodes.label: BREAKING: cluster wire frames the tagged JSON tree (#450)
nodes.rationale: A bare JSON.stringify silently flattened rich values on the way across the wire; the tagged tree preserves them, and the documentation that claimed cross-node messages travel through the pluggable serializer stack was corrected in four pages per language.

nodes.label: BREAKING: system.terminate() drains /user before stopping it (#663)
ActorSystem.runUntilTerminated() (#549)
nodes.rationale: A service's whole shutdown in one call: it installs SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers and keeps the process alive while it waits, because a Node service otherwise exits before the signal it armed itself for ever arrives.

nodes.label: Bounded, optionally durable dead-letter queue with inspection and replay (#433)
nodes.rationale: Dead letters now also name the actor the message failed to reach on every path - previously the record identified the sender but not the destination, which is the half an operator needs.

nodes.label: BREAKING: projection handler-failure recovery strategy (#650)
nodes.rationale: A projection previously retried a poison event forever, so one undeliverable event stalled the whole read side indefinitely.

nodes.label: PersistentActor can be fenced with a lease (#1166)
nodes.rationale: Nothing stopped two live instances of one persistence-id after a partition; a lease makes the second instance fail to start rather than interleave writes into the same journal.

nodes.label: Ring-buffer-backed mailbox queues (#408)
nodes.rationale: A deep backlog no longer costs more per message than a shallow one - the previous queue's per-message cost grew with depth, so an actor that fell behind fell behind faster.

nodes.label: BREAKING: object-storage bodies bound to their storage key (#612)
nodes.rationale: Neither authenticator said anything about where a body lived: AES-GCM's tag and the HMAC both cover the bytes and stop there, so an attacker with bucket write access could replay an authentic body onto another key and load() returned the requested pid with the body's state. The storage key now enters subtle.encrypt as additionalData and, length-prefixed, ahead of the framed bytes in the HMAC input, recorded by a new FLAG_CONTEXT_BOUND manifest bit so older bodies keep decoding.

nodes.label: BREAKING: WebSocket transport frame cap applies in both directions (#373)
Security scanning and policy: CodeQL, bun.lock advisory gate, CycloneDX SBOM, SECURITY.md (#539)
nodes.rationale: The repository had never been statically analysed and had no security policy, while the security issue template told reporters to check a SECURITY.md that had never existed - so anyone following the instruction either disclosed in public or gave up. The policy also writes down the scope boundary a generic policy cannot carry: plaintext cluster TCP is a documented default, not a vulnerability, while a documented mitigation that fails to deliver is one.

nodes.label: Flake program: nightly quarantined multi-node suites and test:stress harness (#290, #538)
nodes.rationale: Three multi-node suites are skipped in CI via ACTOR_TS_SKIP_FLAKY_MNS because Bun on hosted runners cannot respawn functional worker threads, so a green CI check says nothing about them; the nightly runs them with the flag off and carries an explicit exit criterion. The stress harness drops the skip flag from the child environment by default, since a harness that inherited it would report a reliable pass rate over exactly the tests known not to be reliable.

nodes.label: restartOnTermination latch on the cluster singleton (#637, #1175)
nodes.rationale: Both reconcile paths decided whether to spawn from 'I am the host and have no child', which cannot tell a terminal stop apart from never having started - survivable while LeaderChanged was the only trigger, not survivable once every up/down transition reconciles. The opt-out is therefore state on the manager, checked ahead of the membership question so it also gates the lease.

nodes.label: BREAKING: core-only root export plus per-subsystem subpath exports (#414, #1001)
nodes.rationale: The root barrel re-exported every subsystem, so importing ActorSystem parsed everything; sixteen subsystem barrels now sit next to ./testkit, and the default Fastify backend loads lazily (#1005).

nodes.label: Multi-sink logging architecture (#1150-#1161)
nodes.rationale: The logger wrote to exactly one place; it now fans one record out to many destinations. BatchingSink is the bounded, batched, retrying base every slower-than-memory sink extends, and the shipped set covers FileSink, OtlpHttpSink, GelfSink, ParseableSink, LokiSink, SeqSink, SplunkSink, SyslogSink and a sentrySink() factory. A transform hook applied once before fan-out gives redaction a single seam.

nodes.label: BREAKING: every HTTP backend caps a request body at the same 1 MiB (#357)
nodes.rationale: Express and Hono each hardcoded 10 MiB while Fastify used a different bound, so the same route accepted different payloads depending on the backend; all three now answer 413 with the same text/plain body, and Express refuses an over-long declared Content-Length before reading a byte.

nodes.label: BREAKING: HttpClient deadline, response-size ceiling and own redirect policy (#602, #625)
nodes.rationale: The client buffered a whole response with no ceiling and inherited the platform's redirect behaviour, so it never saw the hop that actually answered; the hop budget drops from 20 to 5 and the bounds can no longer be disabled from the caller's side.

nodes.label: BREAKING: CSRF compares whole origins and defaults to the __Host- cookie prefix (#604, #605)
nodes.rationale: csrfProtection and requireSameOrigin compared bare hosts, so scheme and port were ignored and a same-host attacker on another port passed.

nodes.label: BREAKING: getFromDirectory enforces symlinks: 'within-root' on every filesystem hop (#575)
nodes.rationale: The confinement check ran once, against the path a request named, so a symlink encountered later in the walk escaped the root unchecked.

nodes.label: BREAKING: a recorded gossip frame cannot be replayed while its sender is still a member (#112)
BREAKING: an HMAC integrity tag can no longer be stripped to skip verification (#579)
nodes.rationale: FLAG_INTEGRITY_HMAC lived in the body manifest, which the attacker also controls, so clearing the flag removed the check instead of failing it - the classic never-trust-a-client-supplied-integrity-field defect.

nodes.label: Kubernetes lease hardening: construction validation, release reporting, bounded expiry trust (#596-#600)
nodes.rationale: KubernetesLease.release() discarded a failed DELETE, liveness believed the previous holder's expiry claims without bound, and LeaseMajority's release-on-abandon fired from the timeout branch while the acquire it meant to undo was still in flight.

nodes.label: BREAKING: Cassandra CQL identifiers are validated, not concatenated (#614-#616)
BREAKING: rejected connection URLs are reported redacted (#590, #592)
nodes.rationale: OptionsValidator.url() echoed the offending URL, password included, into the error message and thence into logs; redactUrlCredentials and redactedUrlLabel are exported so callers get the same treatment. A later fix made the redaction linear - a hostile redirect could otherwise block the event loop for 484 ms (#1198).

nodes.label: BREAKING: a unary gRPC call is bounded by the configured deadline (#577)
CI supply-chain hardening: SHA-pinned actions and scoped credentials (#585, #621, #622)
nodes.rationale: All 32 uses: references across 11 workflow files were mutable tags; Pages deploy credentials were granted workflow-wide, and the README-badge push shared a job with the whole devDependency tree.

nodes.label: Prototype-chain hardening across HOCON, MIME, CBOR and CRDT decoding (#589, #608, #581, #767)
nodes.rationale: Four independent paths descended with bare property access or assigned decoded keys with out[key] = value, so __proto__ and inherited properties were reachable from untrusted input; DEFAULT_MIME_TYPES gained a null prototype because freezing blocked writes and said nothing about reads.

nodes.label: BREAKING: the default mailbox is unbounded again (#1148)
nodes.rationale: Reverses the bounded-by-default decision of #310; a silently dropping default surprised more deployments than the unbounded growth it was meant to prevent, and every mailbox now reports its drops rather than only the one the framework built (#1149).

nodes.label: Constants placement rule (#1142)
nodes.rationale: src/ held roughly 300 module-level SCREAMING_SNAKE constants across 130 files with no rule, which produced duplicates: a heartbeat interval declared twice, two independently-introduced redraw caps, a rebuilt ATS1 magic prefix, one path-traversal denylist per module. A four-step ordered placement rule now decides where each lives.

nodes.label: EventStream channels can be kind-discriminated types (#1143)
nodes.rationale: Matching was instanceof-only, so a plain tagged object could not be a channel; one faulty subscription also no longer breaks the bus for everyone else (#1010).

nodes.label: Collision predicate on every random-id helper (#1141, #1146)
BidirectionalMap<K, V> (#1035)
nodes.rationale: A reverse index written by hand is two structures that can disagree; it is also the first framework class the tagged JSON tree knows about, so it round-trips through every store. Sharding uses it to resolve entities and regions by index instead of scanning.

nodes.label: BidirectionalMultiMap<L, R> (#1037, #1199)
nodes.rationale: The many-to-many sibling of BidirectionalMap, for the shape a subscription registry has; the receptionist, the pub-sub mediator and the broker base all index their subscribers through it. leftSize/rightSize were added later so the collections count participants, not only pairs.

nodes.label: BREAKING: CborSerializer carries the same rich types as the JSON tree (#1036)
nodes.rationale: Map, Set, BidirectionalMap and BidirectionalMultiMap used to fall through to something wrong rather than something absent; the encoder also no longer overflows the stack on a cyclic object or writes bytes it cannot read back.

nodes.label: Avro and Protobuf serializers (#73)
nodes.rationale: Schema is brought by the caller (an avsc type, a compiled descriptor); serializerCodec adapts any byte-native Serializer into a migration Codec so a SchemaRegistry can hold it.

nodes.label: TcpServerActor and shared TcpFraming (#158)
nodes.rationale: Closes the one half of the raw-TCP API that was missing - listening - and moves the three framing strategies plus their two size caps into a module shared with TcpSocketActor.

nodes.label: JetStream Key-Value and Object Store actors (#74)
Stable-observation cluster bootstrap and selfElection (#148)
nodes.rationale: A node may only declare itself the first member of a new cluster once the contact-point set has been stable for a while, so a cold start of N nodes does not form N single-node clusters.

nodes.label: gRPC client-streaming call mode and grpc.health.v1 service (#4, #5)
BREAKING: the cluster wire protocol's discriminator is kind (#494)
nodes.rationale: The framework had three spellings for one concept - t on the cluster wire, type elsewhere, kind in the typed API; type collides with the TypeScript keyword, so kind became the single project-wide convention, carried into the examples' WebSocket protocols too.

nodes.label: BREAKING: a restart stops the actor's children (#634, #635)
nodes.rationale: A restart replaces the Actor instance while the cell and its child map survive, so children of the old instance outlived it; a resumed actor's children are now resumed with it for the same reason.

nodes.label: BREAKING: persistenceId is validated before it becomes a storage key (#133)
nodes.rationale: PersistenceIdValidator rejects an empty id, an over-long one, and path-traversal segments - a persistenceId is caller-supplied and lands directly in a filesystem path, an object key or a SQL identifier.

nodes.label: CRDT payloads validated before merge (#699, #720-#724, #767)
nodes.rationale: decodeCrdt throws on a malformed peer value and every call site is a wire boundary, so a malformed value is dropped rather than escalated; the decoder also stopped recursing once per nested ORMap level, which let a gossip frame exhaust the stack or freeze the event loop.

nodes.label: Gossip claims need authority, not a high version number (#562, #564, #572, #573, #912)
nodes.rationale: The merge was decided purely by version magnitude, and wire handlers credited the payload's self-declared sender rather than the authenticated connection it arrived on; a cluster hello identity is now bound to the TLS peer certificate, because mTLS decided whether a peer belonged in the cluster but nothing decided who it was.

nodes.label: Prometheus cardinality capped per metric family (#131)
nodes.rationale: A label value derived from user-controlled input - a URL path, a header, an id - is an unbounded series generator; bucketize(value, allowed) maps it onto a fixed allow-list.

nodes.label: BREAKING: the HKDF info parameter is required for client-side encryption (#108)
nodes.rationale: EncryptionConfig.info was optional, so the domain-separation input to key derivation could be silently absent; reEncryptObjectStorage gained newInfo for context rotation and registration now rejects a missing or blank info eagerly.

nodes.label: BREAKING: redirect() rejects off-origin targets (#125)
nodes.rationale: The helper wrote the caller's URL into the location header unchecked; redirectExternal(url, status?) is the separate, deliberate off-origin hop.

nodes.label: BREAKING: the two cluster-wide subscriber registries are bounded and watched (#137, #139)
nodes.rationale: Receptionist gained maxSubscribersPerKey and a total cap, DistributedPubSub's Subscribe takes an optional replyTo, and a refused Subscribe is answered rather than discarded - a silent refusal is indistinguishable from a lost message.

nodes.label: Cluster membership is capped and housekeeping is configurable (#138, #841)
SQLite persistence sets an explicit busy_timeout (#124)
BREAKING: Props is gone from the public API (#547)
nodes.rationale: Spawning takes the actor class or a factory directly and per-actor configuration is an ActorOptions third argument; the closure form spawn(() => new MyActor()) was a leftover from the Props era that read as noise at every call site.

nodes.label: BREAKING: idle entities passivate by default after 5 minutes (#892)
nodes.rationale: passivation-idle shipped as 0ms, so nothing ever passivated until an operator noticed; empty shards now passivate too, since a shard actor otherwise outlived its entities indefinitely.

nodes.label: BREAKING: names starting with $ are reserved, anonymous actors get random suffixes (#895, #897, #900, #126, #134)
nodes.rationale: ActorPath accepted any string and a path is rendered into logs, so a forged name was both a path-forging and a log-injection vector; sequential $1/$2 anonymous names were also predictable, which matters wherever a path becomes an address.

nodes.label: BREAKING: the cluster TLS listener actually requests a client certificate (#565)
nodes.rationale: requestCert hard-defaulted to false in both the Node and Bun adapters, so a configuration that read as mTLS authenticated only the server half.

nodes.label: BREAKING: persistence stores no longer silently corrupt rich payload types (#888, #889)
nodes.rationale: Every journal, snapshot store and durable-state store wrote payloads through a plain JSON path, so NaN, Infinity, -0, undefined in value positions and framework classes came back wrong; the in-memory reference stores now round-trip through the same codec as the real backends, so dev and prod agree.

nodes.label: BREAKING: ReplicatedEventSourcedActor no longer takes a Cluster, and replicaId has a default (#833)
nodes.rationale: Both parameters existed only because the actor could not reach its own Cluster; an actor can now, so the arguments became noise.

nodes.label: NoDeadConfigKeys guard and the published reference.conf page (#653, #834, #754)
nodes.rationale: Whole config blocks - sharding, cluster, remote, system, worker-cluster, coordinated-shutdown, http - shipped in reference.conf and were documented while nothing read them; a test now asserts every leaf is reachable from ConfigKeys and read by something in src/, with a KNOWN_DEAD_KEYS list that must name the issue that will remove it.

nodes.label: BREAKING: a shard is a real actor - Region to Shard to Entity (#511)
nodes.rationale: A shard used to be nothing but a number key in ShardRegion's maps, so it had no lifecycle of its own to supervise, passivate or introspect.

nodes.label: SingletonKey and ShardKey - typed, class-declared identities (#523)
nodes.rationale: A singleton's name and its message type used to be two unlinked facts; ClusterSingleton.start() now returns an ActorRef and SingletonHandle is gone, so addressing a singleton takes one concept instead of three.

nodes.label: DevTools - embeddable web UI for a running system
nodes.rationale: The bundle under src/devtools/generated is generated but committed, and a stale one is valid TypeScript, so CI gates it on a source-hash rather than a byte diff - the bytes vary with the OS and Bun release that produced them.

nodes.label: Cloudflare D1, DynamoDB, MongoDB, MS SQL Server and libSQL/Turso backends (#438, #398, #397, #399, #400)
nodes.rationale: Each ships the full journal + snapshot store + durable-state triple; the relational ones are thin subclasses over the shared base, so a new SQL backend is a dialect plus a pool adapter rather than a rewrite.

nodes.label: Relational persistence base layer and SqlDialect (#389)
nodes.rationale: RelationalJournal / RelationalSnapshotStore / RelationalDurableStateStore plus a dialect seam; LazyStore shares the lifecycle - lazy connection, memoized init, one-shot schema preparation, ownership-aware teardown - so closing one store no longer tears down a pool another store still holds.

nodes.label: BREAKING: framework actors moved from /user to grouped /system paths (#509)
nodes.rationale: Framework-owned actors sitting under /user made a user-space census wrong and made shutdown ordering accidental; /user is now drained before /system starts stopping.

nodes.label: BREAKING: abbreviations spelled out across all identifiers (0.11.0 and 0.12.0)
nodes.rationale: Type, class, file, method, field, generic-parameter and local names use full words - Command, Message, Acknowledgment, Context, Connection - with two exemptions only: single-letter loop variables, and names mirroring an external API or an established domain acronym. WebSocket also became the single-cap Websocket spelling.

nodes.label: BREAKING: runtime floors raised to Node >= 24 and Bun >= 1.3
nodes.rationale: Node 20 reached end-of-life in April 2026 with no more security fixes; @types/node is pinned to the support floor rather than the newest major so framework code cannot accidentally use a Node-26-only API.

nodes.label: Package-health CI: publint, arethetypeswrong, knip (#416)
nodes.rationale: Three failure modes the test suite structurally cannot see, because they are properties of the published package rather than of the running code.

nodes.label: One declaration form per job: interface for contracts, type for data (#503, #508)
nodes.rationale: An interface states a contract someone implements and extends reads as a hierarchy, where an intersection only reads as conjunction; a data shape states a value's layout, and there type composes with the union aliases the project already uses.

nodes.label: Cassandra journal: LWT-serialized append (#475)
nodes.rationale: CassandraJournal.append did a plain read-modify-write, so concurrent appends silently lost events; the lightweight-transaction path can be opted out of, with the serial consistency governing the Paxos phase exposed as an option.

nodes.label: OptionsValidator and OptionsError (#274)
nodes.rationale: A declarative-but-code validator layer for the XOptions pattern; validation runs once at consume time on the merged settings, so the builder, a plain object and HOCON are all covered and cross-field rules see final values. Check helpers are a no-op on undefined, so an unset optional always passes and required-ness stays where it was.

nodes.label: CORS, CSRF and security-header middleware suite (#353)
Static file serving, MIME registry and streaming bodies (#354)
Typed WebSocket routing and WebSocketClientActor (#1)
nodes.rationale: A websocket(path, actorRef) directive plus the typed client half; the legacy frame-level WebSocketActor API was removed outright rather than deprecated, per the pre-1.0 hard-cut rule.

nodes.label: Fluent options builders framework-wide (#346, #348)
nodes.rationale: Every configurable thing gets one XOptions.ts with three exports - the plain type, the fluent builder, and a union alias that is both a type and a value - kept in naming lockstep: builder method withX, field x, HOCON leaf x, with no divergence.

nodes.label: Bounded mailbox becomes the default (#310)
nodes.rationale: An unbounded mailbox is an unbounded memory sink under overload; this decision was later reversed in 0.15.0 (#1148) because a silently dropping default surprised more deployments than it protected.

nodes.label: HTTP route middleware framework, BearerTokenAuth and IpAllowlist (#312)
Cluster.bootstrap({ name }) and the quality-of-life API shortcuts
nodes.rationale: One-call cluster setup plus method forms - ref.ask, system.spawnTyped, system.http - replacing the free-function equivalents, which were removed rather than kept as aliases.

nodes.label: Public documentation site with full German translation
nodes.rationale: Every page is mirrored 1:1 under a de/ tree with identical code samples and translated prose, so a content change is only finished when both languages move together.

nodes.label: DistributedData quorum writes and reads (#81)
nodes.rationale: Consistency levels local / majority / all; reads merge incoming responses into the local replica before answering, and a timeout rejects the write while the local apply still stands and gossips.

nodes.label: ClusterClient and ClusterClientReceptionist (#86)
nodes.rationale: A lightweight outside-in handle with contact-point failover; a ClusterClient is not a peer, so it deliberately no longer learns why an ask failed inside the cluster.

nodes.label: migrateBetweenJournals and reEncryptObjectStorage (#70)
nodes.rationale: Operational tooling for rolling migrations; the journal copy later had to be fixed to preserve a compacted source's sequence numbers instead of renumbering from 1 (#630).

nodes.label: MultiNodeSpec and ParallelMultiNodeSpec test harnesses
nodes.rationale: An in-process N-role cluster, plus a worker-thread variant for tests that need true parallelism - the variant that Bun on hosted CI runners later could not sustain, which is why three suites are quarantined.

nodes.label: PersistentFSM - finite-state machine over event sourcing
KubernetesLease, lease-guarded singleton/coordinator, and LeaseMajority
nodes.rationale: An external lease is the tiebreaker a purely membership-based resolver cannot have; the four resolvers KeepMajority / KeepOldest / KeepReferee / LeaseMajority differ in what authority they consult, not in what they do with it.

nodes.label: Schema migration chain, codec registry and master-key rotation
nodes.rationale: Rolling-deployment-friendly event/snapshot/state adapters plus an in-process schema registry, and AES-256-GCM master-key rotation with a re-encryption sweep; ambiguous key rings are rejected and the version space warns before it runs out.

nodes.label: CRDT core and Replicated Event Sourcing
nodes.rationale: GCounter, PNCounter, ORSet, LWWRegister, MVRegister and the map variants, plus durable DistributedData so CRDT state survives a full cluster restart. ORSet tags are minted from entropy rather than a per-replica counter, because a guessable tag is a forgeable one.

nodes.label: Observability bridges: prom-client registry and OpenTelemetry tracer
BrokerActor base with reconnect and the three phases of broker actors
nodes.rationale: One base carrying exponential-backoff reconnect and subscription replay; reconnect backoff was later jittered so a fleet no longer retries in lockstep after a broker restart (#652).

nodes.label: Object-storage persistence: ObjectStorageBackend, snapshot and durable-state stores
Cache abstraction and the HTTP cache middleware
nodes.rationale: One Cache interface across in-memory, Redis and Memcached; setIfAbsent carries a hard per-key atomicity guarantee on every backend, which is what makes acquireLock(cache, key, ttlMs) a usable mutual exclusion primitive.

nodes.label: HTTP service stack: the directives DSL
HOCON config: parser, ENV interpolation, Duration and Size types
Cluster fabric: TCP / in-memory / worker-thread transports, sharding, pub-sub, resolvers, seed providers
Actor core: Actor, ActorSystem, ActorCell, Guardian, supervision, mailboxes
Typed Behaviors DSL
nodes.rationale: A functional facade over the OO API rather than a separate runtime, so both styles share one cell, one mailbox and one supervision model.

nodes.label: TestKit: TestProbe, ManualScheduler and the ask/retry patterns

hyperedges.label: Mechanisms preventing two authorities for one thing
Bounding untrusted input at every transport boundary
Pre-1.0 naming and API hard cuts
